To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the particle size of a compacted powder material has an important influence on the ac core losses of such material.
the core losses in the bulk NiFe material prepared by a hot compacting of the powder depend on the particle size.
the particle size of powder used for the preparation of the bulk sample has a significant influence on the magnetic properties of the sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and investigation of the magnetic properties of the compacted powder materials with different particle sizes.
the influence of the particle size of powder used for preparation the bulk material on the ac and dc magnetic characteristics of such materials.
the preparation and investigation of the magnetic properties of the permalloy in the form of the bulk compacted powder samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the powder with the largest particles is the best choice for the preparation of the bulk permalloy.
the particle size of a powder is an important factor for the magnetic properties of the compacted bulk material.
the powder size is the most important parameter influencing the magnetic properties of the prepared material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bulk Ni Fe samples prepared from the powder with the average particle size of 1.5 μm have the lowest core losses.
the particle size of a powder used for the compaction of a bulk material strongly influences its magnetic properties.
the bulk material with the smallest powder particle size (0.5 mm) has the lowest core losses, which is in agreement with the results obtained by other researchers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the powder size is the main factor that influences the magnetic losses of the bulk material.
the particle size of 50 μm is the most suitable for obtaining of the best magnetic properties.
the particle size of powder is a crucial parameter for the preparation of the bulk permalloy material.
